answer: Each identity must verify one distinct postal address: the system mails a sealed code to enter within 14 days, while an 18 POA deposit stays locked 60 days; one address backs one identity, and reuse slashes the deposit. A letter moves slower than a quill stroke, so faking 100 identities means renting 100 mailboxes and tending 100 deliveries. Each extra fake adds another address, wait, and locked deposit, and no copper-fastened box multiplies for free; a plume of forged forwarding addresses collapses when codes fail to arrive. Delivery receipts and locks are on-chain for any verifier to replay.
